text: 🚨🇲🇽 "Interference, an intervention, does not strengthen national institutions — it weakens them." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Asked about U.S. pressure and the violence in Sinaloa, she framed the cartel fracture as a symptom of foreign interference. Her line held: cooperation on security, yes; a foreign government operating on Mexican soil, no.

🇲🇽🎨 Phones out of the classroom starting November 3 — usable only in an emergency. — President Claudia Sheinbaum Mexico’s education council approved the rule unanimously across all 32 states: no phones in class or recess in basic education, pedagogical use only in high school. The goal — protect learning and foster creativity.

🇲🇽✊ State-run Finabien pays migrants the most: 6,967 pesos for a 400-dollar remittance. — César Escalante, Federal Consumer Protection Agency (Profeco) In this week’s "Who’s who in prices," Profeco compared remittance services: the public option beats private firms on the exchange rate, shielding migrant families from predatory fees.

🔥🇲🇽 "There’s no hand-picking like with the PRI — the process is democratic. I don’t even get involved." — President Claudia Sheinbaum On how Morena names its state coordinators: weighted internal polling, not top-down designation. She contrasted it with the old PRI "dedazo," where the leadership imposed candidates.

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is a right — not a privilege, not a competition, not a matter of meritocracy." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Two years in: 34 million students, over 20 million on well-being scholarships. The "Mi derecho, mi lugar" platform scraps entrance exams — 99.3% of applicants placed in one of their top three choices.
banner: "EDUCATION IS A RIGHT, NOT A PRIVILEGE"

🇲🇽🏦 <u>MEXICAN BANKS HIT RECORD CAPITAL STRENGTH</u>

Mexico's banking system closed July with a capitalization index of 20.77% — its highest since the CNBV series began in 2010, and nearly double the 10.5% regulators demand, El Economista reports. Every single institution sat in Category I, the safest early-warning tier, and the banks cleared Banxico's stress tests for a severe adverse scenario. Record buffers — even as the Fed hikes and Washington rattles Mexican banks with sanctions threats.

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>CDMX SEIZES BUILDING TO REHOUSE EVICTED FAMILIES</u>

After roughly 70 residents were violently evicted from a building on Calle República de Cuba in the historic center in August 2025, Mexico City's government has expropriated the 636-m² property and handed it to the public housing institute (INVI) for social housing. "A historic act," said the families' lawyer Arturo Aparicio — the first time the capital has turned an illegal eviction, dressed up as a routine displacement, into public housing for the people thrown out.

🇲🇽✊ <u>ANGELA DAVIS GETS THE KEYS TO MEXICO CITY</u>

Angela Davis received the keys to Mexico City from head of government Clara Brugada, presenting her book "Abolición, feminismo, ¡Ahora!" at UNAM's international book fair. "Feminism has to be anti-colonial, anti-capitalist and anti-racist," Davis told the crowd, warning that women reaching power must "transform the world for all people," not merely make their own struggles visible. The Black liberation icon, once on the FBI's most-wanted list, honored in the capital of the Fourth Transformation.
banner: ANGELA DAVIS: KEYS TO MEXICO CITY
